abstract.para: The storage an &rmt; server requires depends on the number of repositories and architectures that you mirror, and the number of products you enable.

topic.para: Downloaded packages are stored in /usr/share/rmt/public/repo, which is a symbolic link to /var/lib/rmt/public/repo/.

The amount of storage your &rmt; server requires depends on several variables: the number of repositories and architectures that you mirror, and the number of products that are enabled. As a general guide, 1.5 times the total size of all enabled repositories should be sufficient. This is about 200 GB per &sle; release, including all extensions.

note.title: &rmt; mirroring fails when /tmp runs out of space
note.para: When &rmt; mirrors repositories from &scc;, it writes large temporary files in /tmp. If /tmp is too small, or is part of the /root file system, and this file system is small in size, /tmp quickly runs out of space, resulting in a mirroring failure. For more information, refer to .
